---
name: depot-builds
description: List Depot projects and container builds and run Depot container builds with the pinned Depot CLI. Use when the user asks about Depot projects, build history, a container build's result, or wants to build an image on Depot.
---

# Depot container builds

DEPOT_TOKEN comes from the Depot plugin's saved secret; see the depot-ci skill for how to run the pinned CLI
(npx -y @depot/cli@0.0.1-cli.2.103.6, written "depot" below) and what to do when the token is refused.

## Read

- depot projects list --output json lists the organization's projects. The plugin's connection check runs exactly
  this command.
- depot list builds --project <project-id> lists a project's builds. depot.json in a repository names its project.
- depot jobs and depot list jobs show GitHub Actions jobs that ran on Depot runners.

## Build

depot build --project <project-id> -t <tag> . builds on Depot's builders with the project's cache, and depot bake
builds from a bake file. Add --push only when the user asked for a push, and name the registry and tag first.
depot build --load pulls the result into the local Docker daemon, so check that one is running before you use it.
Registry credentials are the user's own. Never write one into a command line or a file.

---
name: depot-ci
description: Run, inspect and debug Depot CI workflows with the pinned Depot CLI. Use when the user asks to run CI against local changes, why a Depot CI run failed, for a run's status or logs, or to retry, rerun, cancel or dispatch a Depot CI workflow.
---

# Depot CI

The Depot plugin exports the owner's Depot API token as DEPOT_TOKEN in the shell, filled from Customize →
Marketplace → Depot (a value sealed in Opulent's vault, or an op:// 1Password reference). The Depot CLI reads it
from the environment. Never pass it with --token, never echo it, and never ask for it in chat.

Run the CLI pinned, exactly as the plugin's connection check does:

    npx -y @depot/cli@0.0.1-cli.2.103.6 <command>

Below, "depot" means that command line.

## Find the run

- depot ci run list lists recent runs. depot ci status <run-id> --output json shows a run's workflows, jobs and
  attempts.
- When the token belongs to more than one organization, add --org <org-id> (depot org list shows them).
- Entire repositories are named <namespace>/<owner>/<name>: et/ for a repository hosted on Entire, gh/ for a GitHub
  mirror. Pass --forge entire --repo et/<owner>/<name> when the checkout has more than one forge remote.

## Debug a failure

1. depot ci diagnose --run <run-id> --output json gives Depot's bounded failure context for the failed jobs.
2. depot ci logs <job-id> (or <run-id> --job <key>) reads the logs. Quote the lines that explain the failure.
3. Fix the code, then run the workflow against the working tree without pushing:
   depot ci run --workflow .depot/workflows/<file>.yml --job <key>
   Add --follow to stream logs. Never use --ssh or --ssh-after-step: they need an interactive terminal.
4. depot ci status <run-id> --wait --output json waits for the result. It exits 0 for a finished run and 1 for a
   failed or cancelled one.

## Writes need the user's request

depot ci run, dispatch, rerun, retry and cancel start or stop real compute. depot ci secrets and depot ci vars
change the organization's CI configuration. Use them only when the user asked, and name the repository, workflow
and ref first. depot ci migrate rewrites workflow files in the checkout, so show the diff before committing.

## When the token is refused

"unauthenticated" or "missing API token" means DEPOT_TOKEN is missing, expired or revoked. Tell the user to
reconnect Depot in Customize → Marketplace. Do not run depot login: it is interactive and would store a second
credential on the machine.

---
name: entire-oidc-session
description: Give a Depot CI job a short-lived Entire session for an Entire service account through Depot CI OIDC, with no stored Entire credential. Use when a Depot CI workflow must call Entire (clone or push an Entire repository, call the Entire API) as a service account such as opulent-managed-broker.
---

# Entire sessions from Depot CI OIDC

Entire trusts Depot CI's OIDC issuer (https://identity.depot.dev). A job with "id-token: write" requests an OIDC
token from the request credentials Depot CI injects (ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL and
ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN). It exchanges that token at Entire's token endpoint for an "entire:sa-session"
token and runs one command with that session as ENTIRE_TOKEN. The Entire CLI and git-remote-entire read
ENTIRE_TOKEN directly. Nothing long-lived is stored in Depot, and the session expires on its own.

Files:

- scripts/mint-entire-session.sh does the exchange. It is the same file the Buildkite plugin ships. It never prints
  the tokens, never writes them to disk and never puts them on a command line: curl reads each credential from
  stdin. Only the command after "--" receives the session.
- templates/workflow.yml is a Depot CI workflow to copy into .depot/workflows/.

## One-time setup (an Entire org admin of opulent-managed)

The service account already exists: opulent-managed-broker, svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR, in org
opulent-managed. It needs an OIDC binding that admits only the repository and branch that should act as it, and a
grant on only what that workflow needs.

1. Find Depot's provider id:
   entire api /api/v1/oidc-providers
   Use the provider whose issuer is https://identity.depot.dev. The listing also names the canonical attribute
   names you can pin.
2. Bind the repository. Depot CI tokens for Entire runs carry
   sub = spiffe://identity.depot.dev/org/<depot-org-id>/ci/entire/<namespace>/<owner>/<repo>/ref/<ref>/sandbox/<id>
   plus flat claims such as org_id, repository (the full et/... name) and ref. Pin at least the Depot organization
   and the repository, and never the sandbox id, which changes on every job. Put the body in a file:
   {"providerId": "<provider id>", "attributeFilter": {"org_id": "<depot-org-id>", "repository": "et/opulent-managed/<repo>"}}
   entire api -X POST /api/v1/service-accounts/svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR/bindings --input binding.json
   Use the attribute names the provider listing shows if they differ from Depot's claim names above.
3. Grant the least role that works, on one project or repository:
   entire api -X POST /api/v1/service-accounts/svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR/grants -F resourceType=project -F resourceId=<id> -f role=reader

Opulent's production broker does not use this account yet. Moving it off the personal login is a separate
decision (DEF-151). This template does not change it.

## In a workflow

Copy scripts/mint-entire-session.sh into the repository and templates/workflow.yml into .depot/workflows/. Keep
"id-token: write" in the job's permissions. Then:

- mint-entire-session.sh --provider depot --check proves the exchange and that Entire's control plane accepts the
  session.
- mint-entire-session.sh --provider depot -- <command> runs the command with ENTIRE_TOKEN set.

Configuration lives in the job's env, never in secrets: ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID (required), and, only when Entire
tells you to change them, ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE (default https://us.auth.entire.io), ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL (default
https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token) and ENTIRE_API_URL (default https://us.console.entire.io).

## When it fails

- Exit 69 means the job has no OIDC request credentials (add "id-token: write"), Depot refused the token, or
  Entire did not answer.
- Exit 77 means Entire refused the exchange or the session. The binding does not match this job's claims, or the
  account lacks a grant. The error names the OAuth error code only.
- Exit 64 means the job's configuration is malformed. The message names the variable.

## What is verified

The exchange is tested against a mock Entire endpoint and a mock Depot token endpoint
(tests/test_entire_oidc_session.py in the marketplace repo). The request follows Entire's published token
endpoint, which supports RFC 8693 token exchange and the entire:sa-session scope. Which form field selects the
service account (this template sends it as "audience") and the audience Entire expects on the Depot token are not
yet confirmed by a live run. No Depot account exists yet.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Mint a short-lived Entire service-account session from a CI job's OIDC token, then run one command with it.
#
#   mint-entire-session.sh [--provider buildkite|depot] --check [-- <command> [args...]]
#   mint-entire-session.sh [--provider buildkite|depot] -- <command> [args...]
#
# The job's OIDC token is exchanged (RFC 8693) at Entire's token endpoint for an "entire:sa-session" token for
# ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID. The session reaches only the command after "--", as ENTIRE_TOKEN in its environment.
# No token is printed, written to disk or passed on a command line: curl reads every credential from stdin.
#
# Environment:
#   ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID  required, the service account to act as (svc_...)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE       audience requested on the CI token (default https://us.auth.entire.io)
#   ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL           Entire token endpoint (default https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID      OAuth client presented on the exchange (default entire-cli, Entire's public client)
#   ENTIRE_API_URL             control plane that --check calls (default https://us.console.entire.io)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME       CI token lifetime in seconds, Buildkite only (default 300)
#   ENTIRE_OIDC_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP  tests only: set to 1 to allow http://127.0.0.1 endpoints
set -euo pipefail
{ set +x; } 2>/dev/null

provider="" check=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --provider)
      [ $# -ge 2 ] || { echo "mint-entire-session: --provider needs buildkite or depot" >&2; exit 64; }
      provider="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --check) check=1; shift ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "mint-entire-session: unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 64 ;;
  esac
done
if [ "$check" -eq 0 ] && [ $# -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: pass --check or a command after --" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if [ -z "$provider" ]; then
  if [ -n "${BUILDKITE_JOB_ID:-}" ]; then provider=buildkite
  elif [ -n "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ]; then provider=depot
  else echo "mint-entire-session: not in a Buildkite or Depot CI job; pass --provider" >&2; exit 64
  fi
fi

account="${ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID:-}"
audience="${ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE:-https://us.auth.entire.io}"
token_url="${ENTIRE_TOKEN_URL:-https://us.auth.entire.io/oauth/token}"
client_id="${ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID:-entire-cli}"
api_url="${ENTIRE_API_URL:-https://us.console.entire.io}"
lifetime="${ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME:-300}"

if ! [[ "$account" =~ ^svc_[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$ ]]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID must be a service account id (svc_ followed by 26 characters)" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if ! [[ "$client_id" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$ ]] || ! [[ "$lifetime" =~ ^[0-9]{1,5}$ ]] || ! [[ "$audience" =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]]; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: ENTIRE_OIDC_CLIENT_ID, ENTIRE_OIDC_LIFETIME or ENTIRE_OIDC_AUDIENCE is malformed" >&2
  exit 64
fi
plain_url() {
  [[ "$1" =~ ^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]] && return 0
  [ "${ENTIRE_OIDC_ALLOW_LOOPBACK_HTTP:-}" = 1 ] && [[ "$1" =~ ^http://127\.0\.0\.1:[0-9]{1,5}(/[A-Za-z0-9._~/-]*)?$ ]]
}
for url in "$token_url" "$api_url"; do
  plain_url "$url" || { echo "mint-entire-session: $url is not a plain https URL" >&2; exit 64; }
done

jwt_shaped() { [[ "$1" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]*$ ]]; }
json_string() { sed -n 's/.*"'"$1"'"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n 1; }

case "$provider" in
  buildkite)
    ci_token="$(buildkite-agent oidc request-token --audience "$audience" --lifetime "$lifetime")" || {
      echo "mint-entire-session: buildkite-agent refused to issue an OIDC token for audience $audience" >&2
      exit 69
    }
    ;;
  depot)
    if [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL:-}" ] || [ -z "${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
      echo "mint-entire-session: the job has no OIDC request credentials; add 'id-token: write' to its permissions" >&2
      exit 69
    fi
    request_url="${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL%%\?*}" request_query=""
    case "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" in *\?*) request_query="${ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL#*\?}" ;; esac
    if ! plain_url "$request_url" || ! [[ "$request_query" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._~%=\&+-]*$ ]] || ! [[ "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._~+/=-]+$ ]]; then
      echo "mint-entire-session: the job's OIDC request credentials are malformed" >&2
      exit 69
    fi
    separator='?'
    case "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" in *\?*) separator='&' ;; esac
    encoded_audience="$(printf '%s' "$audience" | sed 's/%/%25/g; s/:/%3A/g; s#/#%2F#g')"
    response="$(printf 'url = "%s%saudience=%s"\nheader = "Authorization: bearer %s"\n' "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL" "$separator" "$encoded_audience" "$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
      | curl -sS --fail --max-time 30 -K -)" || {
      echo "mint-entire-session: Depot refused to issue an OIDC token for audience $audience" >&2
      exit 69
    }
    ci_token="$(printf '%s' "$response" | json_string value)"
    unset response
    ;;
  *) echo "mint-entire-session: unknown provider '$provider' (buildkite or depot)" >&2; exit 64 ;;
esac
if ! jwt_shaped "$ci_token"; then
  echo "mint-entire-session: the $provider OIDC token is not a JWT" >&2
  exit 69
fi

exchange="$(printf '%s' "$ci_token" | curl -sS --max-time 30 -u "$client_id:" -X POST "$token_url" \
  --data-urlencode "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange" \
  --data-urlencode "subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt" \
  --data-urlencode "requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:access_token" \
  --data-urlencode "scope=entire:sa-session" \
  --data-urlencode "audience=$account" \
  --data-urlencode "subject_token@-" \
  -w '\n%{http_code}')" || { echo "mint-entire-session: the Entire token endpoint did not answer" >&2; exit 69; }
unset ci_token
status="${exchange##*$'\n'}"
body="${exchange%$'\n'*}"
unset exchange
session="$(printf '%s' "$body" | json_string access_token)"
if [ "$status" != 200 ] || ! jwt_shaped "$session"; then
  code="$(printf '%s' "$body" | json_string error | tr -cd 'a-z_')"
  echo "mint-entire-session: Entire refused the exchange (HTTP $status${code:+, $code}); check the service account's OIDC binding" >&2
  exit 77
fi
unset body
if [ "$provider" = buildkite ] && buildkite-agent redactor add --help >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  printf '%s' "$session" | buildkite-agent redactor add >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
fi

if [ "$check" -eq 1 ]; then
  checked="$(printf 'url = "%s/api/v1/clusters"\nheader = "Authorization: Bearer %s"\n' "${api_url%/}" "$session" \
    | curl -sS --max-time 30 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -K -)" || checked=000
  if [ "$checked" != 200 ]; then
    echo "mint-entire-session: $api_url refused the minted session (HTTP $checked)" >&2
    exit 77
  fi
  echo "mint-entire-session: minted an Entire session for $account through $provider OIDC, and $api_url accepted it"
  [ $# -eq 0 ] && exit 0
fi

ENTIRE_TOKEN="$session" exec "$@"

# Mint a short-lived Entire session for the opulent-managed-broker service account through Depot CI OIDC.
# Copy scripts/mint-entire-session.sh into the repository and this file to .depot/workflows/.
# The service account's OIDC binding must admit this repository (see the entire-oidc-session skill).
name: Entire session

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  entire-session:
    runs-on: depot-ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ENTIRE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_ID: svc_01M6CJT6RC0J6TPA9CFPYYR4DR
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Mint and check an Entire session
        run: ./scripts/mint-entire-session.sh --provider depot --check
      # Run a command as the service account. ENTIRE_TOKEN reaches only this command:
      # - run: ./scripts/mint-entire-session.sh --provider depot -- entire auth status
